# FluxFiles

> FluxFiles is an MIT-licensed, embeddable file manager for PHP 8.1+. You run one FluxFiles server next to your app; your backend mints a short-lived JWT per user, and the iframe UI (opened by the JavaScript SDK or a framework adapter) lets that user browse, upload and pick files on your own storage: local disk, AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, any S3-compatible store or SFTP. FluxFiles keeps no user database and makes no calls to the vendor.

This file is for developers and AI assistants integrating FluxFiles into an app (https://llmstxt.org). If you are changing FluxFiles itself, read `AGENTS.md` instead. The same file, with the docs inlined, is served at https://fluxfiles.thai-pc.com/llms-full.txt.

Architecture:

- Core server and iframe UI: the PHP package `fluxfiles/fluxfiles` (or the Docker image) serves a JSON API under `/api/fm/*` and a zero-build UI at `/public/`. Your page embeds the UI in an iframe; the SDK talks to it over `postMessage` and returns the picked file (`file.url`, `file.permanent_url`).
- Token claims are the configuration: every request carries an HS256 JWT signed with `FLUXFILES_SECRET`. Its claims (disks, folder `prefix`, `perms`, `owner_only`, upload size, file types, quota, `role` presets, feature toggles) are enforced on every request. A different user or tenant gets a different token, not a different server config. Every claim and env var is in `docs/reference/CONFIG.md`.
- Metadata stays with the storage: titles, tags, the search index, trash and the audit log live in the storage itself, in a `_fluxfiles/` folder (S3/R2 keep per-file metadata as object metadata). Opt-in, `FLUXFILES_STORAGE_BACKEND=db` keeps that bookkeeping in your own MySQL, PostgreSQL or SQLite instead. A tenant can bring their own bucket (BYOB), with its credentials AES-GCM encrypted inside the token.
- Adapters wrap the same server and token: Laravel and WordPress (PHP, with a route proxy), React, Vue/Nuxt, CKEditor 4/5, TinyMCE and Summernote (JavaScript), token SDKs for Node and Python, and an MCP server for AI agents.
- Paid modules are optional and separate: share links, upload portals, versioning, webhooks, AI vision, OCR, virus scan, backup, C2PA, audit export, SSO, DLP and legal hold are proprietary packages installed with a licence key (`php vendor/bin/fluxfiles update <module>`). Nothing in the MIT core needs them; without a module, its routes answer `501 module_not_installed`. Plans: https://fluxfiles.thai-pc.com/pricing/

Install paths:

- Docker (try it in 30 seconds):

  ```bash
  # One secret (>= 32 bytes), shared by this server and by whatever backend mints your tokens
  echo "FLUXFILES_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32)" >> .env
  docker run -d --name fluxfiles -p 8080:80 --env-file .env ghcr.io/thai-pc/fluxfiles:latest
  TOKEN=$(docker exec fluxfiles php -r 'require "/app/packages/core/embed.php"; echo fluxfiles_token(["user" => "demo", "perms" => ["read","write","delete"], "disks" => ["local"]]);')
  echo "http://localhost:8080/public/index.html?token=$TOKEN"
  ```

  The `?token=` URL is for trying it locally only.
- Composer: `composer require fluxfiles/fluxfiles`, then `php vendor/bin/fluxfiles serve` with `FLUXFILES_SECRET` exported in the same shell. Production web-server configs are in `docs/guides/DEPLOYMENT.md`.
- Laravel: `composer require fluxfiles/laravel`, then register a claims resolver (`FluxFiles::resolveClaimsUsing(...)`); until you do, `<x-fluxfiles>` renders "not available".
- WordPress: install the plugin ZIP from https://github.com/thai-pc/fluxfiles/releases?q=wordpress-v and use Media > FluxFiles, the `[fluxfiles]` shortcode or the block.

Packages (all MIT):

- `fluxfiles/fluxfiles` (Composer): core server, API and UI; `embed.php` provides `fluxfiles_token()`.
- `fluxfiles/laravel` (Composer): `<x-fluxfiles>` Blade component, `FluxFiles::token()`, config, route proxy.
- `ghcr.io/thai-pc/fluxfiles` (Docker): the core server image.
- WordPress plugin (release ZIP, tags `wordpress-v*`): media page, shortcode, block, S3/R2/SFTP and AI tagging settings.
- `fluxfiles` (npm): the JavaScript SDK (`FluxFiles.open({...})`), also served by your FluxFiles server as `/fluxfiles.min.js`.
- `@fluxfiles/react` (npm): `<FluxFiles>`, `<FluxFilesModal>`, `useFluxFiles()`.
- `@fluxfiles/vue` (npm): Vue 3 components and composables, Nuxt 3 auto-import.
- `@fluxfiles/ckeditor4`, `@fluxfiles/ckeditor5`, `@fluxfiles/tinymce`, `@fluxfiles/summernote` (npm): editor plugins.
- `@fluxfiles/node` (npm) and `fluxfiles-token` (PyPI): mint tokens from Node or Python, byte-compatible with the PHP helper. They only mint tokens; the core server still serves the files.
- `@fluxfiles/mcp` (npm): MCP server (`npx -y @fluxfiles/mcp`) that lets an AI agent list, search and read files, and optionally write, through a scoped token.

Mint a token on your backend (all SDKs also accept a `claims` map for any claim by its raw name):

```php
require 'vendor/fluxfiles/fluxfiles/embed.php';
$token = fluxfiles_token(['user' => (string) $user->id, 'perms' => ['read', 'write'],
    'disks' => ['s3'], 'prefix' => "users/{$user->id}/"]);
```

```js
import { createToken } from '@fluxfiles/node'; // reads FLUXFILES_SECRET when `secret` is omitted
const token = createToken({ userId: String(user.id), perms: ['read', 'write'], disks: ['s3'], prefix: `users/${user.id}/` });
```

Security rules for an integration:

- Mint tokens on your server, never in the browser, and keep `FLUXFILES_SECRET` server-side.
- Your token backend and the FluxFiles server must use the same `FLUXFILES_SECRET`, at least 32 bytes; a token signed with another secret is rejected.
- Never put the main JWT in a URL. The SDK and adapters pass it to the iframe over `postMessage`, and API calls send `Authorization: Bearer`. (The short-lived per-file tokens in `/img` and `/stream` URLs are a different, scoped token type.)
- Set `FLUXFILES_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` (CORS) and `FLUXFILES_FRAME_ANCESTORS` (who may frame the UI) to your app's exact origins. If neither is set, any website can frame the UI.
- Keep TTLs short (1 hour by default). A token can't be revoked before it expires except by rotating `FLUXFILES_SECRET`, which invalidates every token.
- Scope each user with `prefix` (and `owner_only` for shared folders) rather than trusting the front end; the server confines every path to the token's prefix.
